The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation):
> "Public Domain
Language: srpski jezik (Serbian)
Translation by: Vuk Karadžić, Đura Daničić
Vuk Karadžić translated the New Testament of the Bible in Serbian, publishing it in Vienna in 1847. Đura Daničić assisted Karadžić in that work, and later added an Old Testament translation in 1867. The whole Bible was published in 1868."
(from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/srp1865/copyright.htm)

Why this is public domain:
Translators: Vuk Stefanović Karadžić, 1787-1864 (New Testament, published in Vienna in 1847); Đuro Daničić, 1825-1882 (Old Testament, 1867; the whole Bible published in 1868). This is the Latin-alphabet text of the same translation as ebible-srp1868. US: published 1847 to 1868, before 1931, so public domain in the United States. Origin country: both translators lived until 1882 at the latest, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 140 years or less, whatever the exact rule of Serbia or Austria.

Sources of these facts:
eBible.org copyright page (https://ebible.org/srp1865/copyright.htm); life dates from English Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vuk_Karad%C5%BEi%C4%87 and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C4%90uro_Dani%C4%8Di%C4%87).

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-srp1865-911dba92, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
